# C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns

*Level 1 card. 7 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly. This includes using slow iteration forms when faster alternatives exist (inefficient construct), recomputing values inside the loop that do not change across iterations (loop-invariant recomputation), performing expensive setup or allocation on every iteration (per-iteration setup), nested loops that could be flattened with better data structures (inefficient nesting), processing all items when only a subset is needed (unfiltered iteration), continuing past the point of usefulness (missing early exit), and modifying collections during iteration (array mutation).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to | use the iteration construct with the least per-element overhead | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes | hoist the invariant expression to just above the loop | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share | create the object once before the loop and reuse it | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m | replace the inner scan with a hash lookup, or halve a symmetric traversal | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled | stop as soon as the outcome is settled, ideally with a primitive that does so | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted | reduce the collection before the expensive step, not after | yes, scales with input |
| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked, which costs correctness first and energy second | iterate over a snapshot, or build a new collection instead of editing in place | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C3.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C3.S7.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
